chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Muthanna, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man is confined (by illness) and he sends his sacrificial animal (hady), and his head hurts before he sacrifices his animal, then he should slaughter a sheep in the place in which he is confined, or he should fast, or give charity. And the fasting is for three days, and the charity is for six poor people, half a Sa' for each poor person.

key_terms.أُحْصِرَ: To be confined or prevented (from completing Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.صَاعٍ: A Sa' (a traditional unit of volume/measure for food)
key_terms.يَنْحَرَ: To sacrifice (specifically by cutting the throat)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim confined by illness before sacrificing their Hady?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a pilgrim confined or prevented from completing Hajj, offering three alternatives: slaughtering a sheep at the site of confinement, fasting for three days, or feeding six poor people with half a sa' each. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical flexibility, allowing the pilgrim to choose the most feasible option while maintaining the spiritual integrity of the pilgrimage despite physical impediments.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Musna, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man is confined (by an illness), so he sends his sacrificial animal. So his head hurts before he sacrifices his animal. So he should slaughter his sheep in the place in which he is confined (by the illness), or he should Fast, or give in charity. And the Fasting, is for three days, and the charity is upon six poor ones, half a Sa’a (approximately 1.5 kg of food), for each poor one’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Nasr from Muthanna’ from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one becomes al-Mahsur (confined) and sends his offering then his head annoys him before the offering is slaughtered, he must slaughter a sheep wherever he is. Alternatively, he must fast or give charity. Fasting is three days and charity is to feed six destitute people each with a half Sa‘ of food.’”
